sources.ref: Kiwi Ears web EQ (https://equalizer.kiwiears.com): the KT1132L register map, how it reads and writes the device, and its band editor

meta.notes: What Kiwi Ears' web app does: 5 peaking bands (its type selector is disabled and every Q write carries type 0), 20 to 20000 Hz in whole Hz, gain ±12 dB and Q 0.1 to 10, both to one decimal, with band frequencies kept strictly ascending (it sorts and rewrites a device that reads otherwise). It has no pre-gain and never touches register 0x66. Applying a preset turns the EQ on, writes each band 50 ms apart, each write waiting for its answer, saves to flash, then closes the device and reopens it 3 s later. Its Clear Flash button (command 0x43) isn't driven by the bridge. These are the app's editor limits, not verified firmware limits. devicePEQ differs: it offers low and high shelves as well (a shelf it wrote reads back on the Allegro Mini, whether it filters as one is unconfirmed), ±10 dB and Q to 5, treats register 0x24 as a preset slot (3 custom, 2 off) and sends writes without waiting for an answer. On the KT1132L, register 0x34 switches the EQ (0x24 answers with a year in ASCII in devicePEQ's captures), good writes answer with flag 0x4f, the fifth band's Q register is 0x3f (0x3e is a phantom register), and the app offers no global gain.
